title: Semantic map of the ethyne model
mappingNote: The original geometry has technical names; the mapping was made from the hierarchy and the geometry and requires a final chemical/visual check. The planes correspond to TRANSPARENT_PARTS_2 and TRANSPARENT_PARTS_1.

parts.name: σ bonds
parts.description: End-on overlap of orbitals along the internuclear axis. Ethyne has one C–C σ bond and two C–H σ bonds.

parts.name: sp hybrid lobes
parts.description: Each carbon atom has two sp hybrid orbitals in a linear 180° arrangement. Its two unhybridised p orbitals are perpendicular to each other.

parts.name: π bonds
parts.description: The two π bonds result from sideways overlap of the unhybridised p orbitals. Their two mutually perpendicular distributions surround the C–C axis.

parts.name: Plane 1
parts.description: The first reference plane shows one orientation of the sideways overlap of the p orbitals. The plane has distinct hatching and a bold outline.

parts.name: Plane 2
parts.description: The second reference plane is perpendicular to the first. It is additionally distinguished by opposite hatching and a different outline.

parts.name: Hydrogen atoms
parts.description: Two hydrogen atoms are located at the two ends of the linear H–C≡C–H molecule.

parts.name: Axes and markers
parts.description: Auxiliary axes, markers and letters support spatial interpretation. They are not additional chemical bonds.
